editorial:
Get ready for another round of traps, blood, and moral choices as Jigsaw’s legacy pulls survivors into a new nightmare. Bobby Dagen, a self-help guru who claims to have survived Jigsaw, becomes the center of attention when a support group gathers around him. But his polished story hides ugly secrets, and soon the deadly games return with even nastier devices. The movie keeps the familiar Saw formula moving fast, with loud tension, quick cuts, and plenty of gross-out moments. If you like horror that mixes crime mystery with survival traps, this one delivers the expected chaos.

The acting is mostly serviceable, with Tobin Bell’s presence still carrying weight even when he is not on screen much. The traps are bigger and more theatrical, which is fun for fans but can feel repetitive if you want deeper scares. Pacing rarely slows down, though some twists feel rushed. Watch it if you enjoy gory horror and franchise closure; skip it if you dislike blood. You can stream in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Bobby’s lies are exposed, and he is forced through a brutal trap that mirrors the story he sold to others. Meanwhile, Hoffman’s deadly battle with Jigsaw’s legacy reaches its end when he is captured and locked in the same bathroom from the first film. The twist reveals that Dr. Gordon, a survivor from the original movie, has been helping Jigsaw all along. He seals Hoffman inside, leaving him to die, while the franchise’s final message lands: Jigsaw’s plan was never just about punishment, but about control and legacy.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gory horror, trap-filled thrillers, and Saw franchise closure.
